sources.citation: Bacchelli & Bird, Expectations, outcomes, and challenges of modern code review, ICSE 2013
sources.shows: Review yields knowledge transfer and awareness as well as defects; understanding the change is the main challenge.
sources.doesNotShow: Anything about how a diff should be presented.

sources.citation: Baum, Schneider & Bacchelli, Associating working memory capacity and code change ordering with code review performance, EMSE 24(4), 2019
sources.shows: 50 mostly professional developers; small changes reviewed more effectively; ordering effect only a tendency.
sources.doesNotShow: That any layout or ordering helps.

sources.citation: Fregnan et al., First come first served: the impact of file position on code review, ESEC/FSE 2022
sources.shows: 219,476 PRs: earlier files get more comments; experiment: one defect type 64% lower odds when its file is last.
sources.doesNotShow: Intra-file presentation effects.

sources.citation: Uwano, Nakamura, Monden & Matsumoto, Analyzing individual performance of source code review using reviewers' eye movement, ETRA 2006
sources.shows: 30 review processes (6 programs, 5 subjects) reveal a 'scan' gaze pattern.
sources.doesNotShow: How a diff should be drawn; small sample.

sources.citation: Alcocer, Cossio Chavalier, Rojas-Stambuk & Merino, An Eye-Tracking Study on the Use of Split/Unified Code Change Views for Bug Detection, IEEE Access 11, 2023
sources.shows: 12 participants; unified view took less visual effort but differences were not statistically significant.
sources.doesNotShow: Any bug-finding advantage; publisher page not retrievable so details not verified.

sources.citation: Myers, An O(ND) difference algorithm and its variations, Algorithmica 1, 1986
sources.shows: Shortest edit script as shortest path in an edit graph; O(ND).
sources.doesNotShow: Which minimal script is easiest to read.

sources.citation: Nugroho, Hata & Matsumoto, How different are different diff algorithms in Git?, EMSE 25, 2020
sources.shows: Myers vs Histogram differ in 1.7-8.2% of commits (14 Java projects, churn) and 6.0-13.3% (10 Java projects, bug-introducing identification); authors judge Histogram better for mining.
sources.doesNotShow: Reader comprehension; Java only; audience is repository miners.

spec.default: Unified, one column, as authored; never converted to split
spec.why: Only direct test (12 participants) leans weakly to unified, non-significant
spec.marxyToday: applied — fence renders as authored (probe-results diff-fence)

spec.default: +, - and space in column one stay in the text and in the clipboard; colour is a second channel only
spec.why: Markers are the information; convention, git verified

spec.default: Tint markup.inserted/deleted lines as second channel; headers and no-newline line in plain code colour
spec.range: theme may set the two colours
spec.why: Convention; no test of colour in diffs
spec.marxyToday: open — scopes.ts maps no diff scope; diff renders monochrome

spec.default: Hang at least 2ch beyond marker column with the 1px rule; never start a row in column one
spec.why: A continuation must not read as +/-
spec.marxyToday: open — wrap rule exists in 04 but not verified for diff fences

spec.default: Render only; when Marxy must compute, line-level histogram in core
spec.why: One Java mining study favours histogram; a thesis reports pathological cases; git default is Myers
spec.marxyToday: open — no diff code in core

spec.default: Plain code, no label at rest; no fabricated diff
spec.why: Old side is absent from the file

spec.default: Rendered text; source copy is a named palette operation
spec.why: Browser and Typora convention; code is never transformed so code copies are exact
spec.marxyToday: applied — design 03 says drag selection copies DOM text

spec.default: Summoned command opening Source mode at the element's data-marxy-s; nothing at rest
spec.why: VS Code and Obsidian offer rendered-to-source
spec.marxyToday: open — showSource exists in app.ts but no element command

spec.default: {path,start,end,exact,prefix,suffix} over source bytes, 32-char context; resolve offsets, then unique context, then unique exact, else fail visibly; fuzzy off
spec.why: Three shipping designs converge; no reader test
spec.marxyToday: open — ReadingPosition is byteOffset+fraction; offsetThroughEdit (restore.ts) handles single-run edits only, measured to fail on multi-site regeneration

spec.default: On external reload, histogram-diff last-read snapshot vs new, mark changed blocks with a summoned margin rule, local snapshot only
spec.why: No study; capability follows from provenance
spec.marxyToday: open — no snapshot, diff or mark

gaps.what: Line numbers and prefix/suffix context in an operation
gaps.detail: OperationInput gives the AST and the range text but not the whole source, so path:L-M and full anchors cannot be computed purely
gaps.proposal: ADR-only PR adding a readonly source: string to OperationInput

gaps.what: Compare two texts (old snapshot vs new, old/new document)
gaps.detail: An Operation receives one Document and returns a splice or clipboard
gaps.proposal: ADR declaring view-state lenses (pure changedRanges(before, after)) outside the operations contract; they never splice

gaps.what: Drag selection resolved to a byte span
gaps.detail: design 03 (D-A2) treats DOM drag as text-only copy; no v1 operation uses span
gaps.proposal: Amend design 03: resolve a drag inside one text node to a span when rendered equals source, else snap to the enclosing block

gaps.detail: Twelve frozen token classes in scopes.ts and tokens.css; no inserted/deleted
gaps.proposal: ADR adding two classes and two tokens, after scripts/registry.json entries

gaps.detail: ReadingPosition (ADR-0018) is frozen at path, byteOffset, fraction, mode
gaps.proposal: ADR amending ADR-0018 with an optional anchor {exact,prefix,suffix}

gaps.detail: Needs a data attribute and possibly a token, plus a shell-held snapshot
gaps.proposal: registry entries first; shell-api gets a local snapshot read/write; token reuse decided at review

gaps.detail: One Document per operation; cross-document is v2 in docs/operations.md
gaps.proposal: Keep as a command through shell-api open; no contract change until v2

taste: Line tint against coloured marker for add/delete
Whether a wrapped diff continuation's rule is sufficient without a marker
changeMyMind: A study showing split or word-level highlighting improves review accuracy would reverse the unified-only default
A test showing histogram and Myers equal for prose would demote the histogram choice
Evidence that readers expect Cmd+C to copy source in a rendered view would reverse the copy default
A measured failure rate of quote-plus-context anchors on regenerated artifacts would justify turning fuzzy matching on
